scope: documented for Vysoká nad Uhom; regional
evidence: The Vysoká municipal history ties the tax list of 1715, 8 households, to the plague of 1709-1710. Belža was resettled after the same plague. Senné had 5 households in 1715 and Iňačovce 8; their sources blame the wars and do not name the plague.
for_the_records: Before any parish register that survives for these villages. It explains why most families of the 19th century arrived after 1720.

scope: regional; one burial count from Solymos
evidence: About 100,000 deaths in Hungary. Zemplén, next door, was among the first counties struck; Ung is not on that list. Nothing found for the three villages. In the records in hand: an entry of about 1831 has a Greek Catholic's son of Viszoka baptised by the Latin-rite priest of Pavlovce with the local priest's consent. That fits a parish without its priest in a cholera year, and proves nothing more. The first count from a village: the Reformed burial book of Solymos has 13 burials in 1831, about six of them in August, against one to eight in each of the following ten years. The illness column has not been read to this agent.
for_the_records: The Senné Roman Catholic burial volume no. 1091 and the Iňačovce Greek Catholic volume no. 381 both cover 1831. The same count there would confirm it.

evidence: A European failure. Nothing village-level found.
for_the_records: Look for a rise in burials of the old and the very young in 1846 and 1847.
Senné and Čičarovce burial volumes cover these years.
The Čičarovce Greek Catholic burial volume no. 182 begins in 1851 and covers Viszoka.

what: Cholera, fifth wave; diphtheria established in Hungary in 1873
scope: regional; one observation in the records in hand
evidence: In one Greek Catholic parish of Zemplén nearly every death entry of summer 1873 gives cholera as the cause. In the records in hand: twins born in May 1873 are both marked dead, with no cause written and a residence that is not one of the three villages.
for_the_records: The first wave for which all three villages have a burial volume in an archive. Causes of death should be written in.

evidence: A penury is documented for the two counties to the west. In the records in hand: a child of Viszoka no. 120 dead at twelve days in March 1879, no cause written.
for_the_records: One infant death is not a pattern. Count the Viszoka burials for 1879 and 1880 in volume no. 182.

evidence: Nothing village-level found. In the records in hand: a child of Jesztreb no. 71 dead at sixteen months in March 1891, the year before, no cause written.
for_the_records: The Iňačovce Greek Catholic index seen has no burials at all, only births and marriages. Whether a burial volume exists for these years is open.

what: Cattle deaths, failed harvests and hunger
evidence: About 600 cows died in Senné in 1940 and the harvests failed until 1942. The church chronicle records hunger in 1941.
for_the_records: Inside living memory and after the filmed registers end.

what: Single infant deaths outside the known waves
scope: observations in the records in hand
evidence: A first child of Viszoka no. 79 dead at six weeks in February 1857; a newborn of Szenna dead in February 1870. No cause written on either.
for_the_records: Ordinary infant mortality, at about three in ten, produces these without any epidemic. Listed so they are not later mistaken for evidence of one.

what: Epidemic hospital and epidemic cemetery at Košice-Barca, wartime
scope: outside the three villages; one record in hand
evidence: A soldier's card held by the Demko agent records a death on 9 March 1915 in the epidemic hospital at Košice and burial in the epidemic cemetery at Barca. The card names no illness. A web search for the cemetery found nothing. In July 1915 the military epidemic observation station at Košice had 3,900 beds. Whether it or its cemetery stood at Barca was not found.
for_the_records: Men of these villages who served in 1914-1915 may have died of disease far from home and be absent from the parish burial book.

what: Child deaths noted on baptism entries of the Iňačovce book
scope: observations in the records in hand
evidence: Deaths are written against baptisms at Jesztreb in 1876 (two), 1885, 1891 and 1894, and at Solymos in 1892. None gives a cause. The 1892 death falls in a cholera year; one death is not a pattern.
for_the_records: The burials are in volume no. 383 (deaths 1860-1898). Counting them by year is now possible in principle.

what: Child deaths noted on baptism entries of the Senné Roman Catholic book
scope: observations in the records in hand
evidence: Deaths are written against baptisms in 1868, 1870, 1875, 1879 (two, on 14 and 15 April), 1886, 1887, 1888 (two), 1893, 1894, 1898 (three), 1902, 1906, 1907, 1908 (four), 1909, 1913, 1918 (29 October) and 1925. No cause is given. They are the deaths in the families whose strips were kept, not a count for the village.
for_the_records: Three in 1898 and four in 1908 are worth checking against the burial volumes nos. 1091 and 1093. The death of 29 October 1918 falls in the weeks of the influenza.
